messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Andrew's RStan feature requests
parts:
Andrew --- for me, the problem isn't that I'm arguing you
shouldn't get these functions, but that I don't quite understand
what you're asking for. I want to create a functional spec
so there's no misunderstandings. This is why people write specs!

We'll have to update it via e-mail because Andrew doesn't want
to use the Wiki. Andrew --- if you want to make changes, can you
just edit what's below and re-send, rather than just sending comments?
That way, we'll at least have one coherent spec we're all working from.

I'm meeting Andrew on Thursday and hopefully we can go over this
and flesh it out into something that an R developer can comment on
and then generate a technical spec, implementation, doc, and tests for.
If anything below is impossible or bad behavior, please let me know before
then.

ANDREW'S FEATURE REQUESTS
========================================================

1. stan_optimize() and stan_sample()
--------------------------------------------------------

1.a. Add a function stan_optimize() that behaves like
stan() in terms of specifying the model (more on that below).

1.b. Deprecate the function optimizing() by printing a warning
to the user.

1.c. Add a function stan_sample() to replace stan().

1.d. Deprecate the stan() function.



2. Make-like behavior (aka "Sebastian's function")
--------------------------------------------------------

When stan_optimize() or stan() are passed a model file, try
the following in order

2.a. check to see if a compiled version of the model exists in
memory that is newer than the model file time stamp, and if so, use that

2.b. check to see if a compiled version of the model exists on the
file system that's newer than the model file time stamp, and if so,
use that

2.c. compile the model and save it in memory, then
if the user has specified a save-file argument, save a version
of the model to that file which can be read in later; suggest
users choose an appropriate suffix based on R conventions.

QUESTION: Do we add any similar functionality for models passed as strings?


3. Verbosity options
------------------------------------------------------
a quiet option that turns off all output.


======================================================


GENERAL QUESTION: Andrew wanted us to standardize names, but I don't see
any suggestions as to what to use and I don't understand which names we're
talking about.

COMMENT: I would very much like to have a binary CRAN install. I'm
tired of all the failed install traffic on the mailing list. Not
that I'm very optimistic given R's gatekeepers.


Some further comments below, mainly for Andrew.


On Jun 17, 2014, at 5:52 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:

> P.S. One intermediate step we could take, while still arguing about the rest, is to standardize default names.

I don't think anyone's arguing here. If there's a spec
we can agree on, then I think any of this behavior will be
easy to build on the primitives.

I think the main issue is figuring out exactly what
you (Andrew) want in terms of functionality and then
figuring out how to do it in a way that's idiomatic
and cross platform and not considered antagonistic by the
R community.

> For example, suppose we run the following function call:

> object <- stan(foo.stan,…)
> or
> object <- stan_optimize(foo.stan,…)

Those are going to need quotes around "foo.stan", right?
One thing that always confuses me in R is where you need
quotes and where you don't. Why in the world does it accept
library(rstan) and not insist on library('rstan')? No idea,
but then that's why I'm not designing the R interface, just trying
to extract your (Andrew's) functional requirements.

> The function can handle this as follows by first looking for a file “foo.stan” in the working directory and an object “foo.stan” in the workspace,

What's the workspace? You mean in memory? And if so,
shouldn't we check memory, then file system, then recompile
in that order? That's what I suggested above.

> Then:

> 1. If the object foo.stan in the working directory exists and has been updated more recently than the foo.stan file (or if there is no foo.stan file), then Stan will just use the foo.stan object as the compiled model and run it.

??? I think you're using "foo.stan" for two different
things here --- the text of the model file and the serialized
(saved to disk) version of the compiled model. Can we at
least give the saved file a different name that follows R
serialization conventions?

> 2. If the object foo.stan in the working directory exists but the file foo.stan has been updated more recently, then Stan will recompile the model from the file and overwrite it as foo.stan in the working directory, then run it.
> 3. If there is no object foo.stan in the working directory but the file foo.stan exists, then Stan will compile the model from the file, save the compiled model as foo.stan, and run it.
> 4. If there is no object foo.stan in the working directory and no file foo.stan, then Stan will spit out an error.

Writing into the working directory is the behavior that
R considers anti-social.


> The above can be default behavior. We can have an option that saves into the directory also.

Saves into what directory? Did my reformulation above capture
what you're after?

>
> But it’s important for me to have some of this functionality.

I'm not sure what the full scope of "this functionality" is. Just
what you listed above?

> As it is, my code is a mess. Running things with 0 chains, etc.,


Why are you running things with 0 chains? There's a model
compile function. Did I miss something?

> it’s horrible.

What else specifically do you find horrible? And how would
you rather see it behave?

> When people use Bugs/Jags, they have to do hack after hack. I don’t want Stan users to be hacking in this way.
>
> Also, we need some verbose options.

I listed the full quiet mode. Is there other verbosity levels
you're after? If so, how should they behave?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Andrew's RStan feature requests
parts: On Tuesday, June 17, 2014 2:12:38 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:

ANDREW'S FEATURE REQUESTS
========================================================

1.  stan_optimize() and stan_sample()
--------------------------------------------------------

1.a.  Add a function stan_optimize() that behaves like
stan() in terms of specifying the model (more on that below).

1.b.  Deprecate the function optimizing() by printing a warning
to the user.

1.c.  Add a function stan_sample() to replace stan(). Rename the sampling() function stan_sample()

1.d.  Deprecate the stan() function.  Deprecate the sampling() function; keep stan() but maybe add an option that defaults to sampling but allows optimizing

2.  Make-like behavior (aka "Sebastian's function")
--------------------------------------------------------

When stan_optimize() or stan() are passed a model file, try
the following in order

2.a. check to see if a compiled version of the model exists in
memory that is newer than the model file time stamp identical to the text representation (R objects in memory do not generally have timestamps), and if so, use that

2.b. check to see if a compiled version of the model exists on the
     file system that's newer than the model file time stamp, and if so,
     use that

2.c. compile the model and save it in memory, then
     if the user has specified a save-file argument, save a version
     of the model to that file which can be read in later;  suggest

users choose an appropriate suffix based on R conventions. Such an argument would have to default to FALSE to avoid being considered malicious by CRAN, which would make it less useful to Andrew. I prefer that they just call save() if they want to.

QUESTION:  Do we add any similar functionality for models passed as strings? Models passed as strings could be covered by 2.a. or by 2.b. if we write a file to the temp directory


3.  Verbosity options
------------------------------------------------------
a quiet option that turns off all output.  Needs to be implemented on the Stan side

======================================================


GENERAL QUESTION:  Andrew wanted us to standardize names, but I don't see
any suggestions as to what to use and I don't understand which names we're
talking about.

COMMENT:  I would very much like to have a binary CRAN install.  I'm
tired of all the failed install traffic on the mailing list.  Not
that I'm very optimistic given R's gatekeepers.

I'm not pessimistic. The stated reason why it didn't work before was because the rstan package was unnecessarily and egregiously large on a disk. If we depend on the BH and RcppEigen packages, then rstan could be a few megabytes. However, if we implement malicious functions, then it won't be allowed on CRAN.

Ben

I don’t think my function idea is “malicious”!  But let me ask a question:  can we have an option to save in a file, so that way users such as me could use it, but it would not be a default?  Then would R not call it “malicious”?  Or is it required that any saving in a file be in a separate function called stan_save() or something like that?  (I’d like stan_save() rather than just save() because I’d like to use default .stan extensions).  By the way, one reason I’d like some sort of auto-save in practice is that Stan crashes R a lot, so the save-the-workspace option isn’t always possible.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Andrew's RStan feature requests
parts:
I am pretty sure CRAN would consider to be malicious any function that writes to a non-temporary directory without the user explicitly requesting so. Maybe a save = TRUE argument to stan() would be adequate, but the usual approach would be for users to call save() if they want to save something. What would a stan_save() function do that is different from the save() function that works for any object?

Ben

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Andrew's RStan feature requests
parts:
Hi, Ben. I was thinking that stan_save() would have certain default behavior, so that the model foo.stan would be saved as foo.rda or whatever. I wanted to make things as smooth as possible. If we had the “save” argument in the stan() and stan_optimize() functions then that might work too, as then these could call the regular save() functions. As I was saying, for me it is awkward to have big objects hanging around in the workspace. Indeed I’ve sometimes been told that it is good R practice to _not_ rely on things being in the workspace but instead to have scripts be self-contained. As a user, I really would like to just use stan() and stan_optimize() without having to use a different stan_compile() function the first time a model is called.
A

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Andrew's RStan feature requests
parts:
RStan is not totally silent. There are some messages on the RStan side that we can make suppressable. And we can currently set refresh to zero to avoid printing the progress. But the informational messages need to get suppressed and also the timings. I think that is it. I guess we need a silent flag for CmdStan, PyStan, etc. to utilize as well.

Ben
